title: Anima is out
body:
**Anima is out on the App Store.** A physical-modeling synthesizer for iPad: no oscillators, just a source of energy exciting a resonating object, ringing out into a room that morphs from delay to reverb.

Every control is a glyph whose shape is its value, so the panel is a picture of the sound. It plays any tuning an MPE controller can send, which makes it the natural companion to Hexatone. Standalone and AUv3, one price, no in-app purchases.

title: Re-deemer is coming to iPad, free
body: Re-deemer is coming to iPad, and it will be free, just like the desktop plug-in. The cassette tape echo is in development as an AUv3 effect with a full native faceplate, so it drops straight into AUM, Logic, and other iOS hosts. No date to share yet; it will be announced here.

title: Pond 1.2: play the emitters over MIDI
body:
Pond's emitters can now be played over MIDI. Flip the Emitters section from Drip to MIDI and they stop dripping on their own and start firing from incoming notes, one emitter per note up from a base note you choose. Play them from a keyboard in the app, or sequence them from your DAW when Pond is a plugin.

- **New emitter rhythms.** Hold an emitter to open a rate menu and pick straight, dotted, or triplet feels, so you can build shuffles and cross-rhythms. Holding to pick means you land on the rate you want instead of cycling past it.
- **Undo and redo in the plugin**, not just the standalone app.

The current build, 1.2.1, also adds a reliability fix: if a saved pond ever got damaged, the app could fail to open, and it now recovers on its own.

title: Anima, a modal synth, launching July 2026
body:
**Anima** is a physical-modeling synthesizer for iPad, and the companion to Hexatone. It is launching this July.

There are no oscillators: a source of energy, a breath or a strike, excites a resonating object, and the sound rings out into a room. Its heart is a modal resonator of 24 tuned modes per voice, so every note lands exactly in tune, including any microtonal pitch Hexatone sends over MPE. Standalone and AUv3.

title: Pond 1.1, a big update to how it plays and feels
body:
Pond 1.1 is here, the biggest update yet to how the pond plays and feels.

- **Per-emitter rates, and drag to move them.** Each emitter keeps its own drip rate now: tap an emitter to change its rate, drag it to reposition it (even several at once, one per finger), and a few at different rates weave into polyrhythms. Each emitter's marker pulses in time with its own drip, so you can see the rhythm at a glance.
- **Undo and redo, in the drawer.** Painting, Generate, Clear, Transpose, emitters, scales: it all steps back and forward.
- **Transpose the whole pond** up or down, right by the scale picker.
- **Six more scales, fifteen in all.** The full set of modes plus harmonic and melodic minor and the Japanese Hirajoshi.
- **Velocity for wave interference.** Set the range with Base, Min and Max; the overlapping waves decide where each note lands.
- **A movable paint bar.** Drag it by the handle to the top or bottom so it never covers the cells you want.
- **Pond follows your host.** As a plugin in AUM, Logic or Cubasis, it now starts and stops with the host transport, so the emitters sit in time with the rest of your session.

title: Hexatone's manual is now on the web
body: The full Hexatone manual is now a page on the site, with a downloadable PDF, covering tunings, the built-in sampler, isomorphic layouts, and MPE. The free in-browser **SFZ Builder** turns a folder of samples into an instrument too.

title: Pond is out on the App Store
body: Pond, a ripple sequencer for iPad, is available now. Drop a stone in the water and let the wave play the notes: tap to send ripples, plant emitters, and watch real wave interference shape the dynamics.
